newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Good catches boost S.Africa's Sea Harvest.
newsitem.headline: Good catches boost S.Africa's Sea Harvest.

text.p: Good summer hake catches and the weaker rand saw South Africa's Sea Harvest Corporation Ltd post favourable half-year results ending March 31, 1997, but it was cautious in its forecast for the full year.
Sea Harvest posted headline earnings per share of 26.4 cents, up from 21.8 cents for the comparable period.

Turnover rose 29 percent from 185 million rand to 238.2 million rand and the improved results were further reflected in an increase in operating profit of 34 percent from 31.2 million rand to 41.8 million rand.
The dividend increased by 11 percent to 10 cents per share payable to registered shareholders.
Managing Director Louis Penzhorn said in a statement the results showed the company's investment in new vessels and upgrading of its plant and facilities was bearing fruit.
He cautioned though that he did not expect to match the growth in headline earnings per share for the full year, due in part to the government's withdrawal of fuel tax subsidies from March 1997.
"This, coupled to a stronger rand, will hamper export opportunities in the months ahead," Penzhorn said.
A satisfactory increase was nevertheless expected, he said.

"We should benefit from higher winter catch rates and will continue to expand our product range by introducing more value-added, quality products in an ongoing effort to capture market share," Penzhorn added.

The 1997 hake total allowable catch has been increased to 153,700 tonnes from 151,000 tonnes in 1996, but the entire industry has been allocated provisional quotas which are four percent lower than 1996. Sea Harvest said it hoped its quota would be at a similar level to last year when the unallocated portion for this year was reviewed by the Quota Board.
